title: MMP v2.0 unencrypted CMB frame
description: Allowed only by an explicitly selected cleartext/migration profile. Core Secure uses encrypted-cmb-frame.schema.json.

protocolVersion.description: OPTIONAL, and never the place a version is agreed. The protocol version is settled once per connection in the authenticated §5.2 handshake (client-hello carries it; CONNECTED means it verified), so it is part of a signed transcript. A frame is transport and is not signed, so a per-frame version is unauthenticated and redundant — a receiver trusting it would be preferring a value anyone can set over one both parties proved. Accepted when present for older senders.

timestamp.description: OPTIONAL. Unix epoch milliseconds at which THIS SENDER emitted THIS frame — it is a transport fact, changes on a re-send, and is not the record's creation time. The timestamp a receiver reasons from is metadata.createdTimestamp inside the record, which is MANDATORY and is covered by the signature, so a relay cannot age a signed record without breaking it. This frame field sits outside the signature: trusting it let a relay make a signed record look arbitrarily old or new, which is why implementations demoted it (see §8.8 verification and the freshness rules). It survives as the interop fallback for a record carrying no signed timestamp, and a conforming receiver MUST prefer metadata.createdTimestamp whenever it is present.
